current_answer: A real commercial expansion with unevenly supported investment and ownership expectations—not an empty market or an inevitable credit crisis. Paid persistence, provider cash, useful older capacity and realized investor gains strengthen the favorable case. The connected cash test now shows how further financing can be feasible, while exposing the trade-off between paying cash to owners and retaining it for debt retirement. Usefulness and a successful financing do not establish that every price or commitment earns enough. Read the connected whole-answer synthesis.
summary: Real paid demand and selective financial resilience. The harder test is whether the cash can satisfy all the claims made on it.
uncertainty: For continuation, obtain the actual A100 term, deployment age and net service economics, plus Austin’s billed-to-collected fees and cash costs. Compare a documented refit with the best feasible continued use rather than assuming every expired contract requires a new generation. Decisive observations and their limits.
